title: Cascadeur
author: Discodowns
selftext:
Anyone used this for animations? The game I'm making has a few non standard animations, and several non human characters, so generic animations won't work. Chat gpt mentioned this to me. Looks interesting, though hate that it's billed annually.

Open to other suggestions for animations. I got Claude to work with blender for a running one. Came out a bit shit but I can prob fix it to a reasonable level. Dunno if it's scalable to use this approach for everything though so was just looking into alternative approaches

comments.author: kokutouchichi
comments.body: It's a fantastic tool for animators but if you're looking to just use it to animate something unconventional and hoping for a one shot prompt solution this definitely isn't it. Cascaduer can supercharge your animation skill but you need to already know how to animate? If that makes sense.

replies.author: Discodowns
replies.body: Yeah I don't really. Have vague idea of keyframes and stuff but im a full stack engineer, no history at all with animation.

replies.author: kokutouchichi
replies.body: Yeah I would say if you were already familiar with animation it would blow your mind but it still has its own learning curve as it's different from Blender and Maya in the way it creates animation sets, etc. but if you aren't familiar with the basics of animation this would probably not be the best software to quickly get some animations on your character for ai gamedev. For regular humanoid characters there are plenty of solutions I think. For unconventional characters you may just have to animate it yourself in Blender for now or rig it somehow and do some motion capture to animation or something. Though both approaches will still require significant manual fixing

comments.author: Upper-Philosophy2376
comments.body:
it's more of an animation clean up tool than an animation tool, think of it as adding a bit of phsics to the animation to make it seem more weighty or believable. It seems it's best uses are for humanoid stuff. 

I think it might be possible to pull animation from videos but I can't remember what that tool was called. I think Nvidia also created a model that generates at least human animation, again I forget what it's called.
